chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Al-Husayn ibn Said has been transmitted by me from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with him - from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Hasan ibn Aban, from Al-Husayn ibn Said. And I have transmitted it from my father - may Allah have mercy on him - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Said.

key_terms.رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: May Allah have mercy on him
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him

ai.seo_question: How is the narration chain for Al-Husayn ibn Said verified in this text?
ai.summary: This passage serves as a critical methodological note by Shaykh al-Saduq, demonstrating the rigorous verification of the *isnad* (chain of transmission) for Al-Husayn ibn Said, a key narrator in the *Kutub al-Arba'ah*. By citing two distinct routes—one through Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan (often identified as the fourth Imam in certain contexts or a prominent scholar) and another through his father, more famous chain via his father (Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Hasan al-Saduq) and the chain of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa—the author establishes the reliability and widespread acceptance of these narrations in Shia scholarship.
